status: historical design context only; implementation-specification.json is the fixed fresh-artifact task authority

identityPolicy.oneToOneExtensions: reuse parent single-column primary key as PK/FK
identityPolicy.foreignKeys: one referenced column; additional cross-row invariants need database constraints/triggers
identityPolicy.nativeIds: separate fields; never substitute internal sequences into FIFA responses
identityPolicy.exceptions: retain existing import hash and migration ledger single-column bookkeeping keys

tables.name: footballers
tables.description: one identity across card versions, with its FIFA ID on the row.
tables.notes:
Canonical native identity is unique among resolved rows for the supported FIFA 21
dataset. Do not assign several footballer rows to one verified identity just to
permit duplicate squad entries. Custom identity exceptions require explicit evidence.

tables.name: teams
tables.description: team identities; each card keeps its own league association.
tables.notes:
Unresolved legacy codes remain recorded in typed compatibility fields or retained
import metadata; do not invent reference rows or treat native zero as an internal FK.

columns.name: code
columns.annotation: UQ         player / manager / consumable / customization / player_pick

tables.name: item_definitions
tables.description: shared identity and canonical native fields for every product.

columns.name: native_resource_id
columns.annotation: own product ID, not a token's preview ID

columns.name: native_subtype
columns.annotation: product-specific subtype; type default if absent

tables.notes:
UQ `(game_year, family_id, native_resource_id)` for resolved canonical resources.
Native asset IDs may repeat across card versions. Current baseline supports one compatible client profile.

tables.name: card_types
tables.description: classification and canonical FIFA rarity/default mapping together.

columns.name: card_level
columns.annotation: bronze / silver / gold or traced category

tables.notes:
`native_rareflag` is not globally unique: different card levels/types can share
the same wire rarity code. Product subtype overrides are explicit in definitions.
Do not use type IDs as native rarity codes.

tables.name: card_designs
tables.notes:
These presentation fields are proposals, not recovered FIFA tunable names.
Map them to actual client assets/settings only with evidence; paths are portable.

tables.name: card_type_designs
tables.description: real type-to-design associations and one default.
tables.notes:
UQ `(card_type_id, design_id)` enforces the original relationship/lookup rule.

One default per type. Keep this association only if several permitted designs
are useful; a simple `card_types.default_design_id` FK can replace it if only one
design per type is supported. It is unrelated to native-ID aliasing.

tables.name: promo_cards
tables.notes:
UQ `(promo_id, definition_id)` enforces the original relationship/lookup rule.

Promo override is a publication input. Resolve it into the card definition's
effective design explicitly; overlapping promos must not change rendering randomly.

tables.name: card_rarity_groups
tables.description: type membership in existing rarity/SBC groups.
tables.notes: UQ `(card_type_id, native_group_id)` enforces the original relationship/lookup rule.

tables.name: player_card_definitions
tables.description: one specific footballer card version and its base stats.

columns.name: native_team_id
columns.annotation: preserve unresolved original code; checked against FK when resolved

tables.notes:
The single `definition_id` FK references the common definition; the deferred
family-state check validates its classification. Attribute columns are
nullable to preserve absent supplied data; render fallbacks stay explicit. The six
typed face-slot columns preserve the supplied native array order. Outfield display
labels such as pace/shooting are mapped through the current contract; goalkeeper
labels must be verified rather than relabeled as outfield values. These are six
columns on the same definition row, not six attribute-row queries. `gk_speed` supplied
metadata and the native in-game slot order remain distinct as in current rules.

columns.name: native_effect_id
columns.annotation: playStyle or traced consumable effect identity

tables.name: customisation_definitions
tables.notes:
Slot compatibility remains sourced from current rules; define additional typed
fields only for traced vanity shapes. Retain their unknown fields as extensions.

tables.name: definition_extensions
clubs
tables.description: existing account/ownership root, preserving supported fields.

columns.name: token
columns.annotation: existing runtime auth state, not a new credential collection

tables.notes:
Remove live `stadium_slot_bindings` JSON only after binding migration acceptance.
Preserve balance constraints and current allocation/identity behavior.

tables.name: items
tables.description: the sole owner and common instance row.
tables.notes:
UQ `(club_id, native_item_id)` preserves club-local native numbering. A deferred
constraint trigger validates `family_id` against the referenced definition family. Persist additional common fields only if inventory establishes
they are independently mutable rather than computed from rules or definitions.

tables.name: player_items
tables.description: changing state of one owned player copy.

columns.name: native_play_style
columns.annotation: unresolved/default compatibility code, validated when resolved

columns.name: duplicate_acknowledged
columns.annotation: persisted acknowledgment only; UI duplicate lookup remains derived

tables.notes:
Owner, definition, family and footballer are derived through the parent item
and player definition; family consistency is validated at commit.
`contract`/`contracts` are rendered
aliases of one field after canonicalization. Style definition must be an applicable
chemistry style; position override must follow application rules.

tables.name: player_stat_values
tables.description: recorded indexed counters, separate from base attributes.
tables.notes:
UQ `(item_id, scope, stat_index)` enforces the original relationship/lookup rule.

Single-column player FK, supported index bounds and nonnegative conversion contract.
Do not guess which slot means goals or games; retain the native index until proved.

tables.name: player_attribute_overrides
tables.notes:
UQ `(item_id, attribute_code)` enforces the original relationship/lookup rule.

Create only for fields the inventory proves can differ on owned copies. Known
codes and the merge rule are constrained; permanent overrides are distinct from
temporary chemistry effects and ordinary definition values.

tables.name: consumable_items
tables.notes:
Quantity is positive for a retained stack; consumption deletes the final empty
stack. Preserve the existing checked subset relation for untradeable quantity.
`amount` and `stackCount` are aliases, not separate quantities.

tables.name: customisation_items
tables.description: owned customization family marker and proved overrides.
tables.notes:
Equipment placement is in bindings. The optional override only applies when an
instance has independent lock state; rule-locked slots do not become editable.

tables.name: player_pick_items

columns.name: state
columns.annotation: unrevealed / revealed / selected, per current lifecycle

tables.notes:
`selected_choice_id` references `player_pick_choices.id`; a deferred constraint
trigger verifies that choice belongs to this token. Delete/retain token state
according to verified selection lifecycle; never create a new choice on replay.

columns.name: wire_representation
columns.annotation: known alias/type/missing distinctions during compatibility transition

tables.name: squads
tables.notes:
UQ `(club_id, native_squad_id)` enforces the original relationship/lookup rule.

Chemistry, star rating and similar values remain derived unless the inventory
proves a stored authoritative scalar is required. Preserve at most one active squad.

tables.name: squad_players
tables.notes:
UQ `(squad_id, slot_index)` enforces the original relationship/lookup rule.

Owned kind requires a matching owned item and definition; concept kind has no
owned reference. UQ `(squad_id, footballer_id)` for eligible slots,
validated through card identity and the deferred ownership/definition checks. Empty slots have no membership row and render
as existing placeholders. Preserve malformed legacy slots in audit/extensions
until disposition, not as guessed owned records.

tables.name: squad_managers
tables.description: manager reference with explicit default/preview support.
tables.notes: UQ `(squad_id)` enforces the original relationship/lookup rule.

tables.name: squad_roles
tables.notes:
UQ `(squad_id, role_code, ordinal)` enforces the original relationship/lookup rule.

Ordinal preserves multiple ordered assignments if the client supports them.
The referenced membership must belong to `squad_id`; render its slot index from
that membership. Deferred checks also cover membership/squad reassignment.

tables.name: squad_tactics
tables.notes:
UQ `(squad_id, mentality)` enforces the original relationship/lookup rule.

Exact native setting names/types are not yet established comprehensively. To
avoid inventing scalar columns, the baseline uses typed setting children below.
Fixed settings may become named columns after the inventory proves their schema.

tables.name: squad_tactic_settings
tables.description: explicit typed scalar settings, provisional shape.
tables.notes:
UQ `(tactic_id, setting_code)` enforces the original relationship/lookup rule.

Exactly one typed value for a valid setting; an inventoried setting registry
constrains codes and types. This table is limited to tactics with unknown schema,
not a generic replacement for all typed gameplay fields.

tables.name: squad_tactic_instructions
tables.notes:
UQ `(tactic_id, instruction_code, ordinal)` enforces the original relationship/lookup rule.

Only activate this shape for actual traced instruction consumers; slot references
must belong to the same squad. Unknown structured fields remain marked extensions.

tables.name: club_slot_bindings
tables.description: one item/default in each equipped stadium slot.
tables.notes:
UQ `(club_id, slot_id)` enforces the original relationship/lookup rule.

Validate slot compatibility against sourced rules. Same-club item/definition
agreement is mandatory. Virtual defaults do not invent owned inventory.

tables.name: squad_extensions
tables.notes:
Other feature extension storage follows the same explicit owner/key/version
pattern and is added only for fields retained by the inventory.

tables.name: market_listings
tables.description: existing market state plus resolved definition linkage.

columns.name: seller_item_id
columns.annotation: historical seller-local ID, not unconditional inventory FK

columns.name: resource_id
columns.annotation: existing native response identity, consistent with canonical definition or preserved alias

columns.name: nation_id
columns.annotation: existing native search projection, not an internal nation FK

tables.notes:
Keep existing native search projections named as they are during compatibility
transition, validating them against the immutable listing snapshot. They are
deliberate indexed projections, not independently writable item authorities.

tables.name: market_player_stat_values
tables.description: indexed counters copied with listed player state.
tables.notes: UQ `(trade_id, scope, stat_index)` enforces the original relationship/lookup rule.

tables.name: market_player_attribute_overrides
tables.description: optional typed instance overrides at listing.
tables.notes:
UQ `(trade_id, attribute_code)` enforces the original relationship/lookup rule.

Current market sells player items. Additional family snapshot tables require an
intentional supported-market expansion. Snapshot FKs must survive seller deletion;
snapshot schema must preserve every transfer-consumed field found in inventory.

tables.name: market_watch
tables.notes: UQ `(club_id, trade_id)` enforces the original relationship/lookup rule.

columns.name: pack_id
columns.annotation: references configured pack identity; policy remains in rules/settings

tables.name: match_settlements
tables.description: existing atomic match claim and immutable retry response.

columns.name: response
columns.annotation: null claim until completion within the transaction

tables.notes: UQ `(club_id, match_key)` enforces the original relationship/lookup rule.

tables.name: player_pick_choices
tables.description: stable revealed choices for one token.

columns.name: is_duplicate
columns.annotation: revealed snapshot flag, not inventory ownership

tables.notes:
UQ `(token_item_id, ordinal)` enforces the original relationship/lookup rule.

Global/local/native choice indexes are rendered from the validated ordered
choice contract; inventory any independent values before collapsing them.
Choice state may have optional typed overrides using the same explicit mechanism
as Draft below. Revealed choices are not rows in club-owned `items` until granted.

tables.name: draft_runs
tables.description: one independent active run per club and Draft mode slot.
tables.notes:
UQ `(club_id, slot)` enforces the original relationship/lookup rule.

`id` identifies the stored run container; `(club_id, slot)` selects the current
mode container. Children reference `run_id`, not club/slot pairs. `run_revision`
tracks lifecycle resets and is not an invented native settlement key. Reset must
replace prior choices/picks atomically and reject stale revisions.

tables.name: draft_picks
tables.description: selected virtual Draft players and manager.
tables.notes: UQ `(run_id, pick_kind, position_id)` enforces the original relationship/lookup rule.

tables.name: draft_choices
tables.description: the currently offered ordered virtual items.
tables.notes:
UQ `(run_id, ordinal)` enforces the original relationship/lookup rule.

Draft item state differing from definition/defaults needs explicit typed fields
or optional named override children before these tables can replace run JSON.
Preserve current virtual contracts/style/position behavior; do not manufacture
owned-item rows for Draft previews.

tables.name: draft_formation_choices
tables.notes: UQ `(run_id, ordinal)` enforces the original relationship/lookup rule.

tables.name: draft_seen_footballers
tables.notes:
UQ `(run_id, footballer_id)` enforces the original relationship/lookup rule.

Only replace `seenAssets` with this table once the mapping/duplicate/order rules
are proved. Add an original-native-code compatibility field if the source contract
requires it; do not discard unresolvable values.

tables.name: objective_counters
tables.notes: UQ `(club_id, stat_code)` enforces the original relationship/lookup rule.

tables.name: objective_claims
tables.notes:
UQ `(club_id, scope, claim_id)` enforces the original relationship/lookup rule.

Uniqueness is per scope/claim; preserve existing response order separately.
Future seasonal resets require an explicit evidenced season key, not a hidden
change to current claim/reward behavior.

tables.name: champions_progress
tables.notes:
Nullable values preserve absent imports and existing renderer defaults. Other
competition keys/fields require inventoried typed tables or explicit retained
extensions; no new match-driven producer is introduced by this design.

tables.name: onboarding
tables.notes:
These existing wire IDs can be zero or refer to historical/virtual state. Add
resolved relationships only where lifecycle evidence supports a live FK.

tables.name: onboarding_kit_choices
tables.description: selected kit definitions and equipped references.
tables.notes: UQ `(club_id, role)` enforces the original relationship/lookup rule.

tables.name: onboarding_stale_loans
tables.notes:
UQ `(club_id, ordinal)` enforces the original relationship/lookup rule.

Preserve original list order/duplicates until the cleanup contract proves they
can be canonicalized. Stale item IDs intentionally have no live inventory FK.

tables.name: sbc_completed
tables.notes: UQ `(club_id, challenge_key)` enforces the original relationship/lookup rule.

tables.name: sbc_squad_counts
tables.notes: UQ `(club_id, challenge_id)` enforces the original relationship/lookup rule.

tables.name: client_data
tables.notes: UQ `(club_id, kind, entry_key)` enforces the original relationship/lookup rule.

tables.name: club_flags
tables.notes: UQ `(club_id, flag)` enforces the original relationship/lookup rule.

tables.name: club_imports
tables.notes: Intentionally independent of club deletion, preserving the one-time import hash.

tables.name: legacy_kv
tables.notes: UQ `(club_id, key)` enforces the original relationship/lookup rule.

tables.name: schema_migrations
tables.notes: Later migration checksums/restricted-role changes remain coordinated with Phase 7.
